# Test 'commit split' with multiple files, allowing multi-way split.

[!unix] skip # pending github.com/creack/pty/pull/155
[!git:2.45] skip # git add -p output is fixed to Git version

as 'Test <test@example.com>'
at '2024-07-08T05:04:32Z'

# setup
cd repo
git init
git commit --allow-empty -m 'Initial commit'
gs repo init
# This fork uses merge-based restacking by default;
# pin the rebase method to preserve this script's original behavior.
git config spice.restack.method rebase


# Create a commit with 3 files
git add file1.txt file2.txt file3.txt
gs bc -m 'Add all features' features

# Create an upstack branch to verify restacking
git add extra.txt
gs bc -m 'Add extra' extra
gs down

# Split: select file1 first, then quit to get remainder.
# The terminal dump is not compared in full:
# input echo position in the pty is timing-dependent.
# The resulting git state is verified below instead.
with-term -final exit $WORK/input.txt -- gs commit split -m 'Add file1'
stdout 'Select hunks for commit 1'
stdout 'Select hunks for commit 2'
stdout 'No hunks selected, stopping split'
stdout 'extra: restacked on features'

# Verify log shows 2 commits
git log --oneline features
cmp stdout $WORK/golden/log.txt

# Verify branch stack
gs ll
cmp stderr $WORK/golden/ll.txt

-- repo/file1.txt --
file 1 content

-- repo/file2.txt --
file 2 content

-- repo/file3.txt --
file 3 content

-- repo/extra.txt --
extra content

-- input.txt --
# First iteration: select file1
await file1
snapshot first
feed y\r
clear
await file2
snapshot second
feed q\r
clear
# Second iteration: quit without selecting anything to trigger remainder commit
await file1
snapshot third
feed q\r
await
-- golden/log.txt --
92f33cd Add all features
38bb2ac Add file1
2123b73 Initial commit
-- golden/ll.txt --
  ┏━□ extra
  ┃   36a4e8c Add extra (now)
┏━┻■ features ◀
┃    92f33cd Add all features (now)
┃    38bb2ac Add file1 (now)
main
